title: Macrina
hookLine: the older sister who taught her brothers Basil and Gregory, and led a community at home

cards: In a whole book of conversation with his older sister, a bishop hardly ever calls her by her name. He calls her the Teacher.
He's Gregory of Nyssa, Basil's younger brother, also a bishop and a deep writer; not yesterday's Gregory, Basil's friend from Nazianzus. His sister was Macrina. She never became a bishop.
She didn't preach at councils. And yet her brother wrote her life, as well as that book.

teach.h: ENGAGED, THEN WAITING FOR THE RESURRECTION.
teach.b: Gregory's Life of Macrina starts at the beginning. She was the eldest child. As a girl, she was engaged to a young man who died before the wedding.
Her family wanted to arrange another match. She refused. In her view, Gregory says, she was still promised to him, a man alive to God, and she would wait for the resurrection.
So she stayed home with her mother and the younger children. Then Basil came home from his studies, and Gregory is startlingly frank about his well-known brother.

teach.h: SHE TOOK PROUD BASIL IN HAND.
teach.b: In paraphrase: Basil came back excessively proud of his skill as a speaker, looking down on everyone important in town. Macrina took him in hand, drawing him toward a simpler life, away from fame, toward God.
The Basil we met two days ago, kissing the sick outside his new city, had a sister behind him. Then Macrina turned her household into a community.

teach.h: MOTHER AND MAIDS AT ONE TABLE.
teach.b: She persuaded her mother to live on equal terms with the women who had been their servants: the same table, the same work, the same prayers. Rank dissolved around the dinner table.
She also raised and taught her youngest brother, Peter, who became a bishop too. At the end of her life, Gregory came to see her, heavy with grief after Basil's death.
She was dying, and she comforted him, and the two talked about the soul and the resurrection.

teach.h: THE TEACHER, AND THE STUDENT BROTHER.
teach.b: He wrote it down as a dialogue, with her as the Teacher, and himself as the student who keeps asking questions. A woman at home, teaching brothers who would go on to teach the church.

how: Orthodox and Catholic Christians honor Macrina as a saint, and Gregory of Nyssa's Life of Macrina and his dialogue with her are read as spiritual classics.

o: the mother of Basil who freed her household's maids
a woman who founded a hospital outside Caesarea
the older sister Gregory of Nyssa called the Teacher

p: came home proud of his speaking

s: Macrina's brother Gregory is the same Gregory as Basil's friend
two Gregorys: of Nazianzus, the friend, and of Nyssa, the brother.

games.q: you're Macrina. your household has servants, and you want to give your life to God at home. what do you do?
o: leave home and go somewhere no one knows you.
keep the household as it is, and pray more.
persuade your mother to live with the servants as equals.
games.why: Gregory says she persuaded her mother to share table, work and prayer with the women who had served them.

practice: Bring to mind someone who was a Macrina for you: an older sister, a cousin, an aunt, a coach, a coworker who showed you the ropes, someone who taught you without a title and maybe took you down a peg when you needed it.
Remember one specific thing they did or said, and hold it. If you pray, thank God for them, by name.

wordCard.voice: Macrina. The older sister of Basil and Gregory of Nyssa, who drew her brothers toward God and led a community at home, and whom Gregory called the Teacher.

orig.note: Greek form of her name, as in her brother Gregory's Life of Macrina.

carryVoice: Your line: the teacher of teachers. No title needed, and no pulpit either. Day seven hundred seventy-five, done.
